lore.title: The Needle
lore.body:
A natural traversable wormhole in the Caul system, found in 2240. Its Reach-side mouth hangs some two million kilometres from Hollin; its far mouth opens on the Inward, near Port Ardent. A transit takes about nine hours through the **throat**, whose geometry shifts and must be read as it is flown: a throat-reader listens, a pilot steers.

It is the only road between the Reach and the rest of humanity.

lore.title: The Narrowing
lore.body:
Every four thousand days — a little under eleven years — the throat tightens. For thirty to forty hours it is impassable: the **Long Night**. Most Narrowings are shallow. Some are deep.

The Narrowing of 1 May 2291 was the deepest ever recorded at the time.

lore.title: Brine-glass
lore.body: An exotic-matter crystal grown in Hollin's deep salt beds: negative energy density, the most valuable substance known, and the reason anyone lives in the Reach. Cutting it is slow and it bursts without warning. Cutters breathe the dust and get **glass-lung**.

lore.title: The harp and the Lectern
lore.body: The **harp** is the instrument that reads the throat: a frame of resonator strings under tension in the **Lectern**, the observatory at the Needle-ward end of the station. The throat's gravitational noise makes the strings sing; a reader listens and charts. It must be tuned to a standard. Ambrose Lyle built it and tuned it to his fork.

lore.title: The Ostrander Concession
lore.body: The Ostrander Concern held the Reach as a mining concession from 2241: towns dug into Hollin's salt, debt-labour shipped out through the Needle, brine-glass shipped back. In 2291 the Board let the Charter lapse and recalled its staff — **the Withdrawal**. The last ship was the *Ostrander Providence*.

lore.title: The Keeping
lore.body: At each Narrowing, crewed ships fly brine-glass into the throat's waist and release it there, to **feed the Needle** so that it reopens. Those who fly are **Keepers**. The first Keeping was flown in 2291.

lore.title: The Draw
lore.body: In the Compact, the nine Keepers of each Keeping are chosen by lot from all citizens between eighteen and forty: names drawn from the brass Wheel in the Compact Hall, sixty days before the Narrowing. A volunteer may be substituted with the High Warden's leave. It is called the Compact's one perfectly fair institution.

lore.title: The Severance
lore.body: The war between the Compact of the Reach and the Shoals Free League, which began in 2602 when the Shoals refused their Draw quota.

lore.title: The Quiet
lore.body: The long collapse after the Severance, in which the Compact ended and nearly every record older than it was lost. The Wardens' books at the Anchor begin in 2741. What happened before is liturgy, songs, and arguments.

lore.title: The Ebb
lore.body: Since the Fifty-Eighth Narrowing the Needle has not opened fully; since the Fifty-Ninth no ship has crossed. And it has begun to give back what was put into it — **Returns**: old ships, coated in glass, drifting out of the mouth into the Ossuary.

lore.title: The Wardens of the Throat
lore.body: The order that reads the Needle and keeps the Keeping, founded by the **First Warden** after the first Keeping. Their motto, from the Founder's Fork: *For Clarity*. They tune the harp to the **Hunger Tone**, sung at investiture.

lore.title: The Liturgy of the Long Night
lore.body:
*The First Warden heard the Needle's hunger, and the Reach answered.*
*We feed the door that it may stay a door.*
*What the Needle keeps, it keeps for us.*

lore.title: Hollin
lore.body: A cold moon of the gas giant Caul: ice over salt over glass. Its towns are dug down into the salt — Tallow first and largest — and lit by Caul-light when Caul is up.
